title: Characteristic ideal of the fine Selmer group and results on $Œº$-invariance under isogeny in the function field case

predicted_errors.error_location: Statement of Theorem 5.1 (Section 5) vs. Theorem 1.6 / Remark 1.7(ii) and the proof of Theorem 5.1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Theorem 1.6 in the introduction assumes "H²_fl(K_∞, E_i[p^∞]) = 0, for i = 1, 2", Remark 1.7(ii) calls "H²_fl(K_∞, E_i[p^∞]) = 0" the analogue of the weak Leopoldt conjecture, and the proof repeatedly uses "The assumption H²_fl(K_∞, E₁[p^∞]) = 0 ...". But the restated Theorem 5.1 in Section 5 says "Also assume that H^1_fl(K_∞, E_i[p^∞]) = 0, for i = 1, 2". The hypothesis of the same theorem is stated with two different cohomological degrees.

The lemma states "|H^1(G, B)| ≤ |B|^d and |H^1(G, B)| ≤ |B|^{d(d-1)/2}" — the same group H^1 appears in both bounds (the second should be H^2). As written the two bounds contradict each other: for d = 1 the second gives |H^1(G,B)| ≤ |B|^0 = 1, while the first gives |H^1(G,B)| ≤ |B|, and the paper later uses the first bound (Remark 2.13) for d = 1, where the stated second bound would force triviality.

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Theorem 5.1 (Section 5), finiteness claims and Euler-characteristic computation
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proof asserts "ker(f₁) and coker(f₁) are both finite" and "for i = 2, 3, ker(f_i) and coker(f_i) are finite", and then computes μ(S(E₂)^∨) − μ(S(E₁)^∨) = log_p[χ(Γ, coker f₁)/χ(Γ, ker f₁)]. But for a *finite* module M over Γ ≅ Z_p one always has |H^0(Γ,M)| = |H^1(Γ,M)|, i.e. χ(Γ,M) = 1 (equivalently, a finite Λ-module has μ = 0). Hence under the stated finiteness the right-hand side is forced to be 1 and ord_p(χ_fl(Spec K, A)) = 0 identically, contradicting the paper's own claim that "if ord_p(χ_fl(Spec(K), A)) is positive, one can obtain examples of elliptic curves with positive μ-invariant". The kernels/cokernels must be allowed to be infinite (p^r-torsion, cofinitely generated) for the theorem to have content.

Definition 2.19 defines χ_fl(S,N) only "whenever the groups H^i_fl(S,N) are finite". For S = Spec(K) with K a function field and A a finite flat p-group scheme, the flat cohomology is typically infinite (e.g. H^1_fl(K, μ_p) = K^×/(K^×)^p, H^1_fl(K, α_p) = K/K^p), so χ_fl(Spec(K), A) appearing in Theorem 1.6/5.1 is in general undefined; the Euler characteristic in [TW11, §5] is taken over the curve (or an open U), not over Spec(K).

The proof writes "0 = (A(L_n) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p)_div → ((A(L_∞)⊗Q_p/Z_p)^{Γ_n})_div → (C_n)_div → 0". Since A(L_n) is finitely generated, A(L_n)⊗Q_p/Z_p ≅ (Q_p/Z_p)^{rank} is divisible, so its divisible part is the whole group and is nonzero whenever the rank is positive; it is not 0. Consequently the subsequent deduction lim→_n ((A(L_∞)⊗Q_p/Z_p)^{Γ_n})_div = 0 is false (the colimit is the divisible group A(L_∞)⊗Q_p/Z_p). The functor 𝔊 picks up the dual of the *quotient by* the maximal divisible subgroup, not the divisible subgroup itself.

The corollary claims "the characteristic ideals of R^S(E/K_∞)^∨ and R^S(E/K_∞)^{∨,ι} ... are equal, i.e. there is a pseudo-isomorphism R^S(E/K_∞)^∨ ∼ R^S(E/K_∞)^{∨,ι}". Equality of characteristic ideals does not imply pseudo-isomorphism of torsion Λ-modules (e.g. Λ/p² and Λ/p ⊕ Λ/p have the same characteristic ideal but are not pseudo-isomorphic). The "i.e." is an invalid logical equivalence.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 6 (Theorem 1.5, Proposition 6.2, Theorem 6.3): 'G = Gal(K_∞/K) is pro-p'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: In the ℓ ≠ p part, K_∞ = K(E[ℓ^∞]) and G = Gal(K_∞/K) is stated to be an open subgroup of GL₂(Z_ℓ). An open subgroup of GL₂(Z_ℓ) contains a copy of Z_ℓ and therefore cannot be a pro-p group for p ≠ ℓ. The hypothesis should be that G is pro-ℓ (equivalently, has no element of order ℓ, as required by the Howson/CSS machinery used). The same mistake appears in §2.8 where the trivializing extension is called 'a p-adic Lie extension'.

The remark argues "the order of the kernel of isogeny equals its separable degree, we get that μ(S(E₂/K_∞)^∨) = μ(S(E₁/K_∞)^∨)". For the purely inseparable Frobenius isogeny the kernel is a non-trivial infinitesimal finite flat group scheme of order q = p^r (only its group of points is trivial); since Theorem 5.1 is formulated with flat cohomology of A = ker(φ) as a group scheme, χ_fl(Spec(K), A) need not be trivial, and the conclusion does not follow from the stated reason. The sentence also conflates the order of a finite group scheme (= degree) with the separable degree.

From the long exact flat-cohomology sequence of 0 → A → E₁[p^∞] → E₂[p^∞] → 0 one gets |ker f₂| = |H^1(A)|·|H^0(E₁)|/(|H^0(A)||H^0(E₂)|) and coker f₂ = ker(H²(A)→H²(E₁)); hence χ(coker f₂)/χ(ker f₂) = χ(H²(A))χ(H^0(A))χ(H^0(E₂)) / (χ(H²(E₁))χ(H^1(A))χ(H^0(E₁))). Equation (11) has the roles of E₁ and E₂ interchanged (χ(Γ,E₁[p^∞](K_∞)) in the numerator, χ(Γ,E₂[p^∞]) in the denominator) and omits the χ(Γ,H²_fl(K_∞,E₁[p^∞])) factor.

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Theorem 5.1: "which can be easily derived from equation (5)"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Equation (5) is Milne's localisation sequence 0 → H^1_fl(U,𝒜[p^∞]) → H^1_fl(K,A[p^∞]) → ⊕_v ... in Remark 2.3, which has nothing to do with the multiplicativity of Euler characteristics in the six-term snake-lemma sequence for f₁, f₂, f₃. The cross-reference is wrong (the relation follows from the unnumbered exact sequence displayed just above).

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix A, Case 1 (equation (14) and surrounding text)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Case 1 is explicitly "Take 𝒦 = K_cyc", yet the displayed Euler-characteristic identity is written entirely in terms of K_∞: "χ(Γ, H²(G_S(K_∞), A)) × χ(Γ, E₁[ℓ^∞](K_∞)) × χ(Γ, H⁰(G_S(K_∞), A)) / (χ(Γ, H¹(G_S(K_∞), A)) × χ(Γ, E₂[ℓ^∞]))", and the following sentence mixes both fields ("As E₁[ℓ^∞](K_∞) and E₂[ℓ^∞](K_∞) ... Therefore, χ(Γ, E₁[ℓ^∞](K_cyc)) = ..."). The notation also switches from g_i to f_i ("χ(Γ, coker(f₂))/χ(Γ, ker(f₂))") although the maps in diagram (13) are g_i.

"Additionally, if know that the growth of the Tate-Shafarevich group Ш(A/Kₙ)[p^∞] is of the kind p^{μ₁·pⁿ+c} ..., then we can conclude that λ = 0". This does not follow: Ж^S(A/K_n) is only a subgroup of Ш(A/K_n)[p^∞], so |Ж^S(A/K_n)| ≤ p^{μ₁ p^n + c}; if μ₁ > 0 this bound is compatible with any λ > 0. Nothing in the stated hypothesis forces the λ-invariant of Ж^S to vanish or its order to stay bounded.

Remark 3.1 claims "The following theorem of [Tan10] shows that ker(S_n^A) and coker(S_n^A) are both finite and bounded independently of n", but the quoted Theorem 3.2 requires A to have "good ordinary reduction at every place in S" where S is the ramification locus, whereas the S fixed in Section 3 is explicitly taken to contain all primes of bad reduction of A. The hypotheses of the cited theorem are therefore not met in the generality in which the conclusion is invoked (and boundedness is only asserted there for d = 1).

predicted_errors.error_location: Remark 2.13 (and its use in Proposition 4.2 / Remark 4.8)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: "Let K_d be a Z_p^d-extension of K ... Then the group E[p^∞](K_d) is finite" is stated for an arbitrary elliptic curve. This fails for constant (isotrivial) ordinary elliptic curves over the arithmetic Z_p-extension K_∞ = K·F^{(p)}, where the étale part of E[p^∞] is defined over constant p-power extensions and E(K_∞)[p^∞] ⊇ Q_p/Z_p is infinite. The cited [BL09a, Lemma 4.3] applies under a non-isotriviality hypothesis, yet Remark 4.8 explicitly offers constant elliptic curves as examples satisfying the hypotheses of Proposition 4.6, whose proof (via Proposition 4.2) relies on this finiteness.

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Theorem 5.1 ("Gal(K_{∞,w}/K_{∞,w}) ≅ ∏_{ℓ≠p} Z_ℓ") and Appendix A, Case 1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The absolute Galois group of the local field K_{∞,w} (a local field of characteristic p with residue field the Z_p-extension of F) is not isomorphic to ∏_{ℓ≠p} Z_ℓ; it is non-abelian and has non-trivial p-cohomology (Artin–Schreier). What is isomorphic to ∏_{r≠ℓ} Z_r is the Galois group of the residue field extension. In the ℓ = p case the deduction "Therefore, ker f_4 = coker f_4 = 0" for p-primary *flat* cohomology cannot be justified by this prime-to-p argument.

The symbol e_n is defined in Theorem 1.1 as (rank E(L_n) − rank E(L_{n−1}))/φ(p^n), but in Remark 1.4 (immediately following) e_n is defined by |Ж^S(A/K_n)| = p^{e_n}, and in Proposition 3.3 by #S(A/K_n) = p^{e_n}. Three incompatible meanings of the same symbol, with no warning, make the statements mutually contradictory as written.

Both entries are the identical paper: Coates, Schneider, Sujatha, "Links between cyclotomic and GL₂ Iwasawa theory", Doc. Math. (Extra Vol.):187–215, 2003. They are cited as if they were distinct sources (e.g. [CSS03a, Lemma 2.5] in §6 and [CSS03b, Proposition 2.13] in Proposition 6.2), which is a duplicated/incorrect reference.

The Carlitz action is given as "t = X^p + tX" (i.e. [t](X) = X^p + tX), but for F a finite field with q = p^r elements the Carlitz module is [t](X) = X^q + tX. The displayed recursion is also incomplete/garbled ("t^n = t)"), so the definition as stated is incorrect except when F = F_p.
